What does each json_tokener state do?

Long image

A

Answer

The tokener keeps one small record per nesting level on a stack. Each record says what the level does with the next byte (state), where it goes after whitespace (saved_state), what value it is building (current) and which object key is pending (obj_field_name). The 27 states are the steps of reading one value. A container never reads its own elements: it pushes a new level for each element and adds the result when that level finishes.

  1. Most states finish by setting saved_state to their next step and state to eatws, so whitespace and comments are handled in one place.1
  2. Fields shared by all levels (pb, st_pos, quote_char and others) hold the token being read right now, such as the text of a string or number.2
  3. A local variable, obj, carries a finished child value from the child's finish state to its parent's array_add or object_value_add.3
  4. Every example on this page is a measured trace of the baseline, taken with a stack dump added at redo_char: in a scratch copy.

Applies tojson-c d2ce61ejson_tokener.c and json_tokener.htraces measured 2026-11-24 with a print at redo_char: (scratch copy, not committed)

1

What data does the state machine keep?

Diagram structure
  • struct json_tokener tok
  • struct json_tokener_srec srec
  • tok → srec · stack, max_depth records
Per-level field (stack[i])What it holds
stateWhat this level does with the next byte
saved_stateWhere eatws sends the level after whitespace and comments
currentThe value this level is building: {} growing to {"a":1}, or a finished 1
obj_field_nameThe key of the member being parsed, from the key's end until the member is added
Shared field (tok)What it holds
depth, max_depthWhich record is the current level; how many records exist (default 32)
pbText of the token being read: a string, key, number, literal or comment
st_posPosition inside true, null, Infinity or the 4 hex digits of \uXXXX
quote_charThe quote that opened the current string or key, " or '
ucs_char, high_surrogateThe code point being decoded; a pending first half of a surrogate pair
is_doubleWhether the number has . or e, so it becomes a double
char_offset, err, flagsBytes read in this call; the result code; the STRICT and UTF-8 options
No real variables
state, saved_state, current and obj_field_name are macros for tok->stack[tok->depth], so they always mean the current level
Fixed array
json_tokener_new_ex(depth) allocates depth records once; push is depth++, pop is depth--
Unused fields
srec.obj and tok->str exist in the structs but the parser never uses them; it hands values over in a local obj
2

How does a level get pushed and popped?

  1. Push

    array and object_value check depth < max_depth - 1 (else error depth), set their own state to array_add or object_value_add, then depth++.

  2. New level

    json_tokener_reset_level sets the new record to state = eatws, saved_state = start, current = NULL, no key. The same byte is then re-checked on the new level.

  3. Child parses

    The child level runs through start and the states for its kind of value, building its own current.

  4. Pop

    The child's finish sets obj to its current, resets the child record, depth--, and re-checks the same byte on the parent.

  5. Parent adds

    The parent is waiting in array_add or object_value_add, so it adds obj to its own current and moves on to eatws, then a separator state.

Because the limit check is depth < max_depth - 1, a depth limit counts values, not containers: json_tokener_new_ex(1) rejects [1].4

3

What do the flow-control states do?

StateWhat it doesNext state
eatwsSkips whitespace. A / outside STRICT mode starts a comment. Any other byte is re-checked in saved_state.saved_state, or comment_start
startReads the first byte of a value and picks its kind: { creates an empty object, [ an empty array; quote, t/f, n, i, digit or - start a string, literal or number. Anything else is error parse_unexpected.eatws (then object_field_start or array), or a value state
finishThe level's value is complete. At depth 0 the call jumps to out: and returns it. Deeper, it pops and hands current to the parent in obj.Parent's array_add or object_value_add
4

What do the comment states do?

Comments are allowed only outside STRICT mode. They leave saved_state untouched, so parsing resumes exactly where it was.5

StateWhat it doesNext state
comment_startAfter /: a * starts a block comment and a second / a line comment; anything else is error parse_commentcomment or comment_eol
commentInside /* */: skips bytes up to the next *comment_end
comment_endAfter a *: a / closes the comment, anything else goes back. A second * is lost here (bug hunt finding 2).eatws or comment
comment_eolInside //: skips bytes up to the newlineeatws

Measured on [/*x*/1]: level 0 stays array as its saved_state through comment_start, comment and comment_end, then eatws hands 1 to array. Every comment byte is also copied into pb, which nothing reads (finding 7).

5

What do the string states do?

StateWhat it doesNext state
stringCopies bytes into pb until the closing quote_char, then creates the string in current. In STRICT mode a control byte is error parse_string.eatws (then finish), or string_escape on a backslash
string_escapeThe byte after a backslash: quote, backslash and / are copied; b f n r t become control characters; u starts a code point. Others are error parse_string.saved_state (string or object_field), or escape_unicode
escape_unicodeReads 4 hex digits into ucs_char, counting with st_pos, then writes UTF-8 into pb. A first surrogate half is kept in high_surrogate.saved_state, or escape_unicode_need_escape
escape_unicode_need_escapeAfter a first surrogate half, expects a backslash. Otherwise writes U+FFFD and re-checks the byte.escape_unicode_need_u, or saved_state
escape_unicode_need_uAfter that backslash, expects u for the second half. Otherwise writes U+FFFD and treats it as a normal escape.escape_unicode, or string_escape

Measured on ["hé"]: string copies h into pb, stops at the backslash, string_escape sees u, and escape_unicode turns 00e9 into é. Then string reaches the closing quote with pb holding hé.6

6

What do the literal and number states do?

StateWhat it doesNext state
nullMatches null or NaN one byte per visit, counting with st_pos. Case is ignored outside STRICT mode. Creates NULL or a NaN double; a mismatch is error parse_null.eatws (then finish)
booleanSame for true and false; a mismatch is error parse_booleaneatws (then finish)
infMatches Infinity byte by byte and creates ±Infinity. The minus sign comes from pb, where number left it.eatws (then finish)
numberCopies digits, -, +, ., e into pb while they fit the number's shape. Then it creates an int64, uint64 or double. STRICT mode checks the RFC grammar first.eatws (then finish), or inf after -I

A literal or number is complete only when the next byte arrives. In the trace of [true], pb holds true] at the moment boolean creates the value, and the ] is then re-checked by the parent.7

7

How is an array parsed?

StateWhat it doesNext state
arrayRight after [: a ] closes an empty array. Any other byte pushes a level for the first element.eatws (then finish), or array_add while the child parses
array_addThe child finished: appends obj to currenteatws (then array_sep)
array_sepA , means another element; a ] closes the array. Anything else is error parse_array.eatws (then array_after_sep or finish)
array_after_sepAfter a comma. Same code as array, but a ] here is a trailing comma, an error in STRICT mode.array_add while the child parses

Measured stack after each byte of [1,[2]]. Each level is shown as state / saved_state / current.

ByteStack after this byte
[ (0)L0 eatws / array / []
1 (1)L0 array_add / array / [] · L1 eatws / finish / 1
, (2)L0 eatws / array_after_sep / [1]; L1 was popped and obj = 1 was appended
[ (3)L0 array_add / array_after_sep / [1] · L1 eatws / array / []
2 (4)L0 array_add / array_after_sep / [1] · L1 array_add / array / [] · L2 eatws / finish / 2
] (5)L0 array_add / array_after_sep / [1] · L1 eatws / finish / [2]; L2 was popped into L1
] (6)L0 eatws / finish / [1,[2]]; L1 was popped into L0
end (7)L0 finish at depth 0: the call returns [1,[2]]

The 1 is not added at byte 1. It is added at byte 2, because the number only ends when the , arrives. While a level waits in array_add, its saved_state is a leftover from the step before; it is overwritten as soon as the level resumes.8

8

How is an object parsed?

StateWhat it doesNext state
object_field_startRight after {: a } closes an empty object. A quote starts a key; even a single quote is accepted in STRICT mode (finding 4). Anything else is error parse_object_key_name.object_field, or eatws (then finish)
object_fieldCopies key bytes into pb until the closing quote, then copies the key into obj_field_nameeatws (then object_field_end), or string_escape
object_field_endExpects :, else error parse_object_key_sepeatws (then object_value)
object_valuePushes a level for the member's valueobject_value_add while the child parses
object_value_addThe child finished: adds obj to current under obj_field_name, then frees the keyeatws (then object_sep)
object_sepA , means another member; a } closes the object. Anything else is error parse_object_value_sep.eatws (then object_field_start_after_sep or finish)
object_field_start_after_sepAfter a comma. Same code as object_field_start, but a } here is a trailing comma, an error in STRICT mode.object_field

Diagram structure
  • Level 0: the object l0
  • Level 1 l1
  • Level 2 l2
  • l0 → l1 · push at 1, key "a" waiting in L0
  • l1 → l0 · obj = 1, added at the comma
  • l0 → l1 · push at [, key "b" waiting in L0
  • l1 → l2 · push at t, first element
  • l2 → l1 · obj = true, appended at ]
  • l1 → l0 · obj = [true], added at }

Measured stack after each byte of {"a":1,"b":[true]}. Each level is shown as state / saved_state / current, plus its key when it has one.

ByteStack after this byte
{ (0)L0 eatws / object_field_start / {}
"a" (1–3)L0 eatws / object_field_end / {}, key a
: (4)L0 eatws / object_value / {}, key a
1 (5)L0 object_value_add / object_value / {}, key a · L1 eatws / finish / 1
, (6)L0 eatws / object_field_start_after_sep / {"a":1}, key freed
"b" (7–9)L0 eatws / object_field_end / {"a":1}, key b
: (10)L0 eatws / object_value / {"a":1}, key b
[ (11)L0 object_value_add / object_value / {"a":1}, key b · L1 eatws / array / []
true (12–15)L0 waiting, key b · L1 array_add / array / [] · L2 boolean / start / NULL, pb = true
] (16)L0 waiting, key b · L1 eatws / finish / [true]; L2 was popped into L1
} (17)L0 eatws / finish / {"a":1,"b":[true]}; L1 was popped into L0
end (18)L0 finish at depth 0: the call returns the object

The key lives in the parent level, not the child: level 0 holds b while levels 1 and 2 build [true].9
